definition: In statistics, machine learning and algorithms, a tensor sketch is a type of dimensionality reduction that is particularly efficient when applied to vectors that have tensor structure.
details: Such a sketch can be used to speed up explicit kernel methods, bilinear pooling in neural networks and is a cornerstone in many numerical linear algebra algorithms.

explainer.lead: A tensor sketch is a dimensionality reduction method that is especially efficient on vectors with tensor structure. It matters because it speeds up explicit kernel methods and bilinear pooling, and underpins many numerical linear algebra algorithms.

tiers.eli5: Instead of storing a huge table, you keep a short summary that preserves what you need to compare things quickly.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply tensor sketches to accelerate explicit kernel computations and bilinear pooling in neural networks. The pitfall is that it is a compression, so the approximation must be validated for the task at hand.
tiers.paperLevel: A dimensionality reduction applied to tensor-structured vectors, used to speed up explicit kernel methods, bilinear pooling in neural networks and numerical linear algebra algorithms. Its limit is approximation error inherent to sketching.

explainer.example: A model with bilinear pooling replaces the expensive explicit pooling operation with a tensor sketch, reducing computation while preserving the comparison it needs.
